# Feature: Page-Delta Observation

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-035
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_interaction_wave2.md`

After every successful browser action the agent is handed a fresh 50-element observation and left to work out, by re-reading it, what the action actually did. FEAT-035 adds a compact, bounded **`delta`** block beside that observation: the URL changed, a dialog named _X_ opened, 12 elements appeared and 3 vanished, focus moved from _Destination_ to the suggestion list. "A dialog named `Search results` opened" steers the next move better than eighty re-listed elements do, and it costs a fraction of the bytes.

Three things make this a real feature rather than a formatting change.

1. **The delta must be true.** Refs are minted by `(role, name, ordinal)` (`agent-controller.ts:391-410`), so same-named controls that reorder between observations **trade ref identities**, and the 50-element model cap can make a perfectly stationary element disappear from the returned list. A delta computed over the model-visible list would routinely report appearances and vanishings that never happened. The delta is therefore computed over an **uncapped semantic fingerprint** derived during the scan that was already being taken.
2. **It must be free.** Memory (Architecture) is explicit: _"Diagnostic work is paid for only on the path that needs it… Assert it by counting the operation in a test, because a silent extra page read is invisible in every other signal."_ Plan §9 repeats it: _"The delta requires no additional page scan."_ Every action tool already takes exactly one post-action observation; the fingerprint is derived inside it, before the model-visible slice, and the count is frozen by a test.
3. **It must never over-claim.** A `PageDelta` says **what changed in the action window**, not that the action caused it (plan §4). Where a bound — a replaced document, a truncated fingerprint, a degraded scan — prevents a definite statement, the delta carries a **completeness marker** instead of a manufactured number.

### What ships in this wave, and what deliberately does not

Plan §12 item 3 closed the brainstorm's open question: **additive**. `delta` ships **alongside** the existing `observation`, and `browser_observe` is **unchanged**. Removing the embedded observation is a later, measured decision, gated on evidence that the delta preserves next-action refs and reduces total context/turn cost **without** increasing `browser_observe` turns. TASK-006 records exactly the evidence that decision needs; this feature draws no conclusion from it, and **claims no token savings** (plan §10).

### Non-negotiable constraints

- **Generalize the differ API, not the identity rule** (plan §7). `packages/core/src/interaction/editee.ts` already diffs two `AgentBrowserObservation`s **by ref** to find which control's value took the typed text. That ref policy is correct for value-flow evidence and stays exactly as it is. Page appearance/vanishing uses the **uncapped semantic fingerprint**. One differ API, parameterized by an identity policy; two policies.
- **No extra page scan, no extra DOM walk.** The fingerprint is derived from data the existing in-page scan already produces, before `buildAgentPageSnapshot` applies `maxInteractables`. Dialog/container identities come from the ancestry walk `computeScope` already performs per candidate — not from a second `querySelectorAll`.
- **Baseline ownership.** The controller retains the fingerprint of the last **model-visible** observation. Internal `observe({trackDigest: false})` calls — `FILL_RESOLUTION_CAP` field resolution, click re-acquisition, identity healing — must **not** silently replace it. This reuses the existing `trackDigest` flag rather than inventing a second one.
- **One delta per top-level tool call.** A `browser_fill_form` batch compares its initial frame with its one final observation; it does not emit one delta per field.
- **No website-specific logic** (memory → General). Every signal is structural: ARIA role, accessible name, group/scope, focus, document epoch, URL. A site name in the differ, the fingerprint, or a fixture body is a bug.
- **A tool result must say what actually happened** (memory → Coding Standards). The delta reports the observed difference and marks its own incompleteness; it never phrases a bounded observation as a definite claim.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does **not** exist, and plan §4 states that **no new relational schema and no Data Modeller pass is needed**. **This feature involves no tables, no columns, no indexes, and no migrations.** The granular model below is the set of **contract shapes**: two in-process types (one private, one model-visible) and one generic differ result. Nothing here is persisted as a new artifact — the delta rides the existing tool result and the existing `tool-calls.jsonl` projection (plan §10).

### Entities & Attributes

#### `ObservationFingerprint` — private change-detection state (never model-visible)

Derived during the existing scan, **before** the model-visible cap. Never returned to the model, never based on refs, never stored on disk.

- `epoch` (`string | null`) — the document marker stamped on `window`. Equal across two fingerprints ⟺ the same document. `null` when the page refused the stamp.
- `url` (`string`) — the page URL at scan time.
- `title` (`string`) — the page title at scan time, already clamped to 300 chars by the snapshot builder.
- `entries` (`ReadonlyMap<string, number>`) — the **semantic multiset** of visible interactables: identity key → occurrence count. Built from the **uncapped** ordered visible list.
- `entryCount` (`number`) — total visible candidates counted, before `entryCap` truncation.
- `truncated` (`boolean`) — `true` when `entryCount` exceeded `FINGERPRINT_MAX_ENTRIES`.
- `containers` (`ReadonlyMap<string, OverlayIdentity>`) — visible dialog/overlay/listbox/menu/grid containers, keyed by their identity key. Derived from the ancestry walk the scanner already performs for `scope`.
- `focus` (`string | null`) — identity key of the focused interactable, or `null` when the active element is not a scanned candidate (body, a non-candidate node, or no focus).
- `degraded` (`boolean`) — `true` when the in-page scan degraded to `[]` (the existing `safeEvaluate` best-effort path), so the fingerprint's emptiness is not read as "the page has no controls".

**Identity key** (the semantic policy): `role`, accessible `name`, `group`, and `scope`, joined with a `U+001F` unit separator (written in source as a Unicode escape, never as a raw control byte) and each part clamped to `IDENTITY_PART_MAX_CHARS`. Deliberately **not** the ref, and deliberately **not** including position or ordinal — an element that moves is the same element, and duplicate identities are handled as multiset counts rather than by ordinal, which is precisely what stops reordered same-named controls from trading identities.

#### `PageDelta` — the bounded, model-visible difference

Emitted as `delta` on **success and partial-success** results only. Every field is omitted when there is nothing to say, so an action that changed nothing produces a near-empty block.

- `url_changed` (`{ from: string; to: string }`, optional).
- `title_changed` (`{ from: string; to: string }`, optional).
- `dialogs_opened` (`OverlayIdentity[]`, optional) — capped at `DELTA_DIALOG_CAP`.
- `dialogs_closed` (`OverlayIdentity[]`, optional) — capped at `DELTA_DIALOG_CAP`.
- `elements_appeared` (`{ count: number; sample?: OverlayIdentity[]; sample_truncated?: true }`, optional) — `count` is the definite uncapped multiset difference; `sample` names at most `DELTA_SAMPLE_CAP` of them.
- `elements_vanished` — same shape.
- `focus_moved` (`{ from?: OverlayIdentity; to?: OverlayIdentity }`, optional) — either side omitted when focus was not on a scanned candidate.
- `complete` (`false`, optional) — **the completeness marker.** Present only when a bound prevented a definite statement; its absence means the block is definite.
- `incomplete` (`DeltaIncompleteReason[]`, optional) — present exactly when `complete` is. A fixed enum carrying no page text.

`DeltaIncompleteReason` is a closed union:

| Reason                    | Meaning                                    | Effect on the block                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `'document-replaced'`     | `epoch` differs between the two frames     | `elements_appeared` / `elements_vanished` / `focus_moved` are **omitted** — a new document's controls are not the old document's controls |
| `'fingerprint-truncated'` | either frame hit `FINGERPRINT_MAX_ENTRIES` | element counts omitted                                                                                                                    |
| `'scan-degraded'`         | either frame's in-page scan degraded       | element counts, dialogs, and focus omitted                                                                                                |

`'no-baseline'` is deliberately **not** a reason: with no prior model-visible observation there is nothing to diff, so the `delta` block is **omitted entirely** and `details.delta_omitted: 'no-baseline'` records why. This is the ordinary state of the first `browser_navigate` in a run.

**Standing bound, documented rather than re-declared per delta:** a container is nameable only when it holds at least one scanned candidate. The delta therefore lists dialogs it observed opening or closing and **never asserts that no dialog is open**. This is stated in the tool descriptions and in the type's JSDoc; emitting it as a per-call reason would add bytes to every result to repeat a permanent property.

#### `OverlayIdentity` — shared vocabulary with FEAT-033

`{ role: string; name: string }`, both page-derived, `name` bounded to `OVERLAY_NAME_MAX_CHARS`. Plan §7: _"a dialog named X opened" is both the most steering-relevant delta and the obstruction signal. The features should share vocabulary for dialog identity._ FEAT-035 **imports** `OverlayIdentity` from `packages/core/src/browser/obstruction.ts` (FEAT-033, which precedes it in the plan's dependency order) as a **type-only** import, and selects the **outermost** container in the bounded ancestry the same way `overlay-dismiss.ts` and FEAT-033's classifier do — so the dialog FEAT-035 says opened is the same dialog FEAT-033 would name as the obstruction. If FEAT-033 has not landed, define the shape in `page-delta.ts` and let FEAT-033 import it; the plan requires **one shape**, not one file.

#### `KeyedDiff<T>` — the generic differ result (plan §7's "one differ API")

- `appeared` (`readonly T[]`) — keys present in `after`, absent in `before` (capped sample).
- `vanished` (`readonly T[]`) — the reverse (capped sample).
- `changed` (`readonly { before: T; after: T }[]`) — key present in both, projection differs.
- `appearedCount` / `vanishedCount` (`number`) — **uncapped** multiset differences.
- `sampleTruncated` (`boolean`).

`diffKeyed(before, after, { key, changed?, sampleCap? })` is the whole API. The **identity policy is the `key` function**, which is the one thing the two callers disagree about:

| Caller                              | `key`                 | Why                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locateEditee` (unchanged behavior) | `entry.ref`           | Value-flow evidence. The caller just typed into a control it holds a live ref for; ref identity is exactly right, and a re-targeted drive must address a ref the port can actually drive. |
| `diffFingerprints` (new)            | semantic identity key | Refs trade identities when same-named elements reorder, and the model cap hides unchanged elements.                                                                                       |

### Relationships

- One `ObservationFingerprint` per `observe()` call. The controller holds two references to fingerprints, never a history: `lastScanFingerprint` (every scan) and `deltaBaseline` (**only** scans where `trackDigest !== false`).
- One `PageDelta` per **top-level tool call** = `diffFingerprints(deltaBaseline at call start, fingerprint of the post-action model-visible observation)`. A `browser_fill_form` batch therefore produces exactly one delta covering the whole call — its initial frame is the page the model last saw, and its final frame is the single `controller.observe()` the batch already takes.
- `ObservationFingerprint` 1:N `OverlayIdentity` via `containers`; `PageDelta` references `OverlayIdentity` in `dialogs_opened` / `dialogs_closed` / element samples / `focus_moved`.

### Indexes & Constraints

**No database objects.** The invariants are type-level and test-enforced:

- `PageDelta` carries `incomplete` **iff** it carries `complete: false` — unrepresentable otherwise.
- A definite `elements_appeared.count` may not be emitted when any `incomplete` reason that invalidates element comparison is present.
- Every bound is a named exported constant with a test that trips it: `FINGERPRINT_MAX_ENTRIES = 1000`, `DELTA_DIALOG_CAP = 5`, `DELTA_SAMPLE_CAP = 5`, `IDENTITY_PART_MAX_CHARS = 120`, `DELTA_MAX_BYTES = 2048` (asserted over the serialized block).
- `ObservationFingerprint` is not exported from any model-visible projection: a boundary test asserts `modelObservation()` and `modelDelta()` outputs contain no fingerprint field and no ref-keyed identity map.

Implementation is multiset-aware: bucket both sides by `key`, then for each key compare counts — surplus in `after` contributes to `appearedCount` (and, while under `sampleCap`, to `appeared`), surplus in `before` to `vanishedCount` / `vanished`, and pairs present on both sides are compared with `changed` when supplied. ### TASK-005: Attribute a fill's navigations, dialogs, and popups to the fill that caused them

- [ ] **Implementation**: Close the leak recorded at `.spec-lite/TODO.md` §"Popup & overlay follow-ups" — _"A popup opened during a fill is attributed to the next action"_ and _"A popup opened during a fill is still not offered for adoption"_ — both marked planned as FEAT-035, and named by plan §13 as subsumed by this feature. `WidgetPort.click/fill/clear/type` return `Promise<unknown>` and every caller discards the `BrowserActionResult` the controller built, so a popup, a JS dialog, or a landing URL produced **by a fill** is either dropped or surfaces on whatever tool runs next — and `recordActionProvenance` never runs for a fill, so the URL a fill navigated to is later refused as `URL_NOT_FROM_EVIDENCE`. Give `browserWidgetPort(controller, now, sink?)` an optional plain collector that accumulates each action's `url`, `title`, `popup_intercepted`, `popup_followable`, `dialog_intercepted`, and `overlays_dismissed`; it is a collector only — **no retry, budget, or ordering semantics**, so FEAT-034 can later wrap it for action accounting without unpicking anything. Add `takeActionMetadata()` to the controller: a **synchronous** drain of the popup/dialog queues and the followable-popup handle, taking **no page read** (memory → Architecture: diagnostic work is paid for only on the path that needs it) — it exists to catch anything that landed after the fill's last port action rather than letting it leak forward. `applyBrowserFill` threads a sink through both the driver path and the secret path and returns the accumulated metadata; `runFillElement` and `runFillForm` then do exactly what `browser_click` already does with an action result: `recordActionProvenance(...)`, then `followSiteOpenedTab(...)` — subject to the **unchanged** provenance, URL-policy, and ethics checks, with no new bypass — then surface `popup_intercepted`, `dialog_intercepted`, `switched_to_new_tab`, and `overlays_dismissed` in the model payload, stripping `popup_followable` exactly as the click path does. When the follow adopts a tab, the post-action observation and therefore the delta are taken on the **adopted** page, which is the page the fill actually produced.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: A fill whose driver click opens a popup reports `popup_intercepted` **on the fill result**, and a subsequent `browser_click` reports **none** — the leak, asserted in both directions. A JS dialog raised during a fill reports `dialog_intercepted` on the fill. A fill that navigates records URL provenance, so a following `browser_navigate` to that URL is **not** refused `URL_NOT_FROM_EVIDENCE`. A same-site popup opened by a fill is adopted and reported as `switched_to_new_tab`, with the delta computed against the adopted page; a cross-site popup is **not** adopted and stays `popup_intercepted`; an ethics refusal leaves the tab unadopted and the result otherwise unchanged. A batch attributes each metadata item to the batch call once, with no duplication across fields. `takeActionMetadata()` performs **zero** page reads, asserted by the TASK-002 counting decorator.

Create `packages/core/src/audit/delta-cost.ts` exporting `summarizeDeltaCost(entries: readonly ToolAuditEntry[])`, which reads `end`-phase entries in `seq` order and returns `{ calls, deltaBytesTotal, deltaBytesMax, observationBytesTotal, followUpObserveCount, followUpObserveRate }`, where a follow-up is a `browser_observe` call whose immediately preceding tool call in the run was a delta-bearing action. This makes the third measurement directly readable from the artifact instead of "someone could compute it", and it is a **reader only** — it changes no behavior and no policy. ## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. FEAT-035 adds no capability, no grant, no confirmation, and no new page action. Every action it observes was already authorized by the tool that performed it.
- **Error Handling**: No new error code, and no change to any existing one. Delta derivation is **best-effort and never fails an action** — it reuses `observeAfterAction`'s existing contract, so a failed post-action read degrades to no observation and no delta rather than converting a successful click into a tool error. `diffFingerprints` is pure and total: every bound it cannot see past becomes a completeness reason, never a throw. FEAT-033's `ELEMENT_OBSTRUCTED` and FEAT-034's verdict ledger are untouched.
- **Logging**: No new sink and no new artifact (plan §10). The delta rides the existing sanitized `tool-calls.jsonl` projection as part of the model payload; the cost fields ride `details`. `DeltaIncompleteReason` is a fixed structural enum carrying no page text. The accessible names inside `delta` are page-derived and pass the same `sanitizeAndBound` chokepoint in `middleware.ts` as every other model-visible field — TASK-004 asserts it rather than assuming it. `ObservationFingerprint` is process-local and is never logged, serialized, or returned; a boundary test asserts it never reaches a model-visible projection.
- **Security**: The fingerprint holds accessible names and values-free identity keys only; it never holds refs, handles, secrets, or resolved values. Sanitization is unchanged, because the delta enters the model through the payload path that already sanitizes.
- **Backward compatibility** (memory → General; plan §8): additive in this wave. No existing result field is removed or renamed, no run directory is rewritten, no workflow YAML is affected, and `browser_observe`'s contract is byte-identical.
